label: Business Central
description: ERP application for business operations. Business Central online and on-premises have different hosting and integration requirements; neither is the Finance and Operations platform.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Business Central is an ERP application; distinguish online from on-premises deployment. The online API hint does not establish hosting mode.

Dependencies
For Business Central online, Power Automate through the Business Central connector is optional. Power BI reporting is also optional and has mode-specific requirements. On-premises Power BI embedding has a documented Entra application-registration requirement; do not generalize it to all deployments.

Risks
Review which business records leave the ERP, the integration identity and the report audience. Connector availability does not prove an approved data flow.

Uncertainty
Hosting mode, integrations and permissions require instance evidence. Neither Power Automate nor Power BI is a universal prerequisite; this guidance does not verify controls.

label: Commerce
description: Commerce application spanning headquarters, storefronts and selected retail components. Distinguish cloud and self-hosted Commerce Scale Unit boundaries; a shared Dynamics hostname does not uniquely identify Commerce.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Distinguish Commerce headquarters, storefronts and cloud or self-hosted Commerce Scale Unit components; do not assign them one assumed operating boundary.

Dependencies
Customer-managed keys are optional. The reviewed F&O support table includes Commerce environment-specific resources but excludes e-commerce CMS and recommendations and qualifies cross-geo components.

Risks
Review key ownership and data flows separately for the environment, content and recommendations. Exclusion from this CMK mechanism does not imply absence of encryption.

Uncertainty
Deployment mode, component inventory and actual key configuration are unknown. Shared cloud.dynamics.com hints cannot identify an app or establish coverage of every retail component.

label: Contact Center
description: Contact-engagement application supporting selected voice and digital channels, with standalone or Customer Service-integrated use. It is not interchangeable with Customer Service or an AI agent.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Identify standalone or Customer Service-integrated Contact Center use and the selected CRM, voice or digital channel. Shared CRM endpoints do not identify this application uniquely.

Dependencies
A selected Copilot Studio agent integration has documented channel/agent licensing, consumption and administrative-role prerequisites; these are not universal Contact Center prerequisites.

Risks
Review conversation content, channel-to-agent transfers, action permissions and the recipient of each result. A connected channel does not authorize every agent action.

Uncertainty
Enabled channels, CRM integration, licensing and effective permissions need confirmation. Model the public Copilot Studio product only when that integration is intended; do not assume an agent from the Contact Center label.

label: Customer Insights
description: Product family containing Customer Insights - Data for unified customer profiles and Customer Insights - Journeys for customer engagement. Select the branch; they do not share one interchangeable storage or deployment boundary.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys are distinct product branches, not a single assumed storage boundary.

Dependencies
Using Data profiles or segments in Journeys involves configured sharing with the Dataverse organization hosting Journeys. Resetting Data changes its instance ID, does not remove external source/lake data and requires sharing to be enabled again.

Risks
Review the audience of unified profiles and the receiving environment. A reset is not proof that connected copies were deleted.

Uncertainty
The selected branch, external stores and sharing configuration are unknown. Keep dependencies conditional and verify actual retention/deletion behavior rather than inferring it from the family ID.

label: Customer Service
description: Customer-service application for cases and service workflows. Voice, routing, Copilot agents and other channel integrations are selected capabilities, not a synonym for Contact Center or Dataverse.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Model Customer Service case workflows separately from optional voice, routing, agents and other channels. A shared CRM hostname is not unique app identity.

Dependencies
The documented Power Platform app-installation path needs a database-backed environment with Dynamics 365 apps enabled when the database was created. Channel and agent setup are additional selected paths.

Risks
Review environment administrators, case-record access and integrations that copy customer content. Successful installation is not an authorization boundary.

Uncertainty
Environment generation, feature enablement, roles and case-data handling are unobserved. Do not assume Contact Center, an agent or external storage is enabled for every Customer Service deployment.

label: Customer Voice
description: Survey and feedback application, distinct from Customer Insights and its Dataverse records. Current lifecycle and provisioning status require product-specific confirmation; this entry is not a retirement or availability assertion.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Customer Voice is a survey/feedback application, not an ordinary Dataverse table or a Customer Insights alias.

Dependencies
Reviewed data-flow documentation distinguishes Microsoft-managed survey-service storage in North America or Europe from local-datacenter Dataverse storage, and describes Microsoft-managed survey-service encryption keys.

Risks
Trace survey content and respondent identifiers through each store. The Dataverse environment's region alone does not describe every feedback-data path or deletion obligation.

Uncertainty
Actual location, retention, sharing and current lifecycle/provisioning status remain to be confirmed. Do not infer retirement, merge this product into Journeys, or claim one deletion clears every copy.

label: Dynamics 365
description: Suite of business applications, not a separately deployed workload. Identify the actual Dynamics application and deployment mode when modeling concrete controls, integrations or storage.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Dynamics 365 is a suite/family. Its documentation index is not a separate deployment artifact.

Dependencies
Choose the actual application or platform branch before specifying installation, identity or data relationships. No universal VNet, storage account or Dataverse dependency applies to every suite member.

Risks
An umbrella node can hide different systems, operators and data destinations. Attribute controls and integrations to the applicable application rather than the suite label.

Uncertainty
The constituent application and hosting mode are unspecified. Ask which workload is intended; do not inherit one application's policies or automatically create every possible backend.

label: Field Service
description: Field-service application for work orders and technician operations. Mobile/offline clients, Resource Scheduling Optimization and IoT integrations are separate selected capabilities.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Field Service is the application; mobile/offline, Resource Scheduling Optimization and connected-device features are conditional paths.

Dependencies
Reviewed installation requires an attached Dataverse store with Dynamics 365 apps enabled. Mobile device requirements and storage demand depend on the client and offline profile.

Risks
Review work-order/customer data copied to technician devices, device access and offline scope. Backend roles alone do not establish the device's data boundary.

Uncertainty
Environment, mobile posture, scheduling and IoT configuration are unobserved. Do not create an IoT resource chain or assume every feature is enabled; shared CRM endpoint hints do not uniquely identify Field Service.

label: Finance
description: Finance application on the Finance and Operations platform, not the platform itself. Distinguish cloud, on-premises and development deployments and their identity and integration paths.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Finance is an application on the shared Finance and Operations platform. Shared cloud.dynamics.com hints do not select an app or hosting mode.

Dependencies
For cloud Finance access, Microsoft Entra ID is the identity provider and users are provisioned into the application instance. This does not describe every on-premises sign-in path or mandate Dataverse integration.

Risks
Review application roles and financial-operation permissions as well as tenant identity, especially for exports and integrations.

Uncertainty
Cloud, on-premises and development topology differ. Instance grants and provisioning routes need current evidence; do not assume an older lifecycle-management route remains available to every customer.

label: Finance and Operations
description: Shared Finance and Operations application platform, distinct from the Finance, Commerce, Human Resources and Supply Chain Management applications. Hosting and controls depend on the selected application and deployment mode.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Finance and Operations is the shared platform, not another application duplicating Finance. Distinguish cloud, on-premises and development boundaries.

Dependencies
For the documented optional customer-managed-key integration, a Power Platform enterprise policy's Entra managed identity receives encryption-key access from the Key Vault administrator.

Risks
Review enterprise-policy ownership, key grants and failure/revocation behavior. One key relationship does not establish coverage of every feature or exported copy.

Uncertainty
Application, hosting mode, CMK support and actual grants are unknown. This is not a mandatory Key Vault dependency for every deployment; shared endpoint hints do not uniquely identify a workload.

label: Human Resources
description: Human Resources application. Distinguish current Finance and Operations infrastructure from historical standalone deployments and selected integrations; a shared Dynamics endpoint is not an HR-generation identifier.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Human Resources deployment generations differ: historical standalone guidance is not the current F&O infrastructure path.

Dependencies
Reviewed deprecation guidance says new standalone projects/production provisioning have not been supported since July 2022. Residency guidance identifies US environment-list storage and possible transfer to the Teams service region when that integration is used.

Risks
Separate employee records from management metadata and Teams data flows. Primary workload region does not describe all processing.

Uncertainty
Generation, migration completion, integration and actual locations need evidence. Apply dated lifecycle statements narrowly; they are not proof of tenant availability or residency compliance.

label: Intelligent Order Management
description: Order-orchestration application using Dataverse/model-driven experiences and published flows. Current production provisioning and entitlement are unresolved; support listings and trial guidance alone do not establish availability.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Intelligent Order Management is an order-orchestration application, not Finance and Operations or a generic database.

Dependencies
Reviewed architecture describes a Dataverse/model-driven application whose published orchestrations compile into Power Automate flows. External providers and analytics remain selected integrations.

Risks
Trace order/customer information, orchestration identities and destinations across systems rather than treating the workflow as one internal operation.

Uncertainty
Current production provisioning, entitlement and lifecycle availability are unresolved. An In Support listing or trial/preview setup guide is not production availability evidence. Do not choose a provisioning route or claim retirement without product-specific confirmation.

label: Project Operations
description: Project-management application with Core, ERP-integrated and manufacturing deployment branches. Dataverse, Finance/SCM integration and dual-write applicability depend on the selected branch.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Identify Project Operations Core, Integrated with ERP or manufacturing use. The CRM endpoint hint does not select a deployment branch.

Dependencies
Core has a Dataverse-side application; ERP-integrated and manufacturing paths extend Finance or Supply Chain Management. ERP integration and dual-write are conditional, not universal dependencies.

Risks
Review where project, resource and financial records are authoritative and which identity can change them across an integration.

Uncertainty
Deployment path and configured integration are unspecified. Do not assume a full ERP stack, dual-write installation or migration guarantee merely from this ID; qualify each relationship with scenario and product evidence.

label: Sales
description: Dataverse-based, model-driven sales application. Sales Insights, LinkedIn, Teams, Copilot and conversation features are selected capabilities or integrations, not the base application's identity.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Sales is a Dataverse-based model-driven application, distinct from Sales Insights capabilities and external sales-data providers.

Dependencies
Dataverse and the Power Apps model-driven platform underpin the app. LinkedIn Sales Navigator requires the documented qualifying entitlement and enablement only when selected.

Risks
Review customer/opportunity record access, external data transfers and the purpose of each integration. Licensing is not evidence of approved configuration or the intended audience.

Uncertainty
Offering, permissions and enabled Teams, Copilot, mail or conversation features are unknown. Do not infer them from the Sales ID or shared CRM hostname; apply lifecycle notices to the specific capability.

label: Sales Insights
description: Capability/solution family within Dynamics 365 Sales, not a universally independent SaaS service. Identify the selected insight feature, entitlement and data-processing scope.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Sales Insights is a capability/solution family inside Sales, not a separately established universal service.

Dependencies
Features require the appropriate Sales environment and entitlement. Limited Sales Enterprise access to sales accelerator, conversation intelligence or predictive scoring does not grant every premium capability.

Risks
Review which conversation/customer data the chosen feature processes and who receives the insight. Installation alone does not prove a configured access boundary.

Uncertainty
Feature, entitlement, enablement and retention are unspecified. Do not invent an independent infrastructure stack, infer retirement from a shared documentation hub, or apply one feature's requirements to the entire family.

label: Supply Chain Management
description: Supply-chain application on Finance and Operations infrastructure. Planning Optimization, warehouse clients and Sensor Data Intelligence are selected features with different deployment and ownership requirements.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Supply Chain Management is the application; planning, warehouse and sensor capabilities do not share one unconditional deployment path.

Dependencies
Reviewed Planning Optimization guidance describes included SCM licensing and an SCM-licensed Entra account for installation. Unified Finance/SCM templates list its add-in; that is template-specific, not proof an existing environment uses it.

Risks
Review planning/operational data, execution identities and permissions for the chosen path. Entitlement or template inclusion does not prove secure configuration.

Uncertainty
Hosting generation, template, warehouse clients and sensor integrations require confirmation. Do not infer customer Azure resources or generalize cloud-template requirements to on-premises deployments.

label: Microsoft 365 Copilot
description: Microsoft 365 Copilot catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft 365 Copilot is the workplace Copilot product, not Copilot Studio, a generic agent host or an Azure OpenAI resource.

Dependencies
The reviewed material identifies Entra user authentication and permission enforcement. Organizational-data-grounded experiences use Microsoft Graph context; that relationship must not be extended to experiences documented as web-grounded only.

Risks
Review which organizational content the acting user can access and what a generated response may disclose to its audience. A model's ability to summarize information is not evidence that existing source permissions or sharing are appropriate.

Uncertainty
The assigned experience, grounding mode, user access and enabled extensions are unknown. Do not infer a customer-managed model, VNet or storage account from the product name. Catalog guidance is not a statement that a particular response, connector or deployment satisfies a control.

label: Microsoft Graph
description: Microsoft Graph catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft Graph is an API boundary; this entry's graph.microsoft.com matcher identifies the commercial/GCC endpoint rather than every national-cloud endpoint.

Dependencies
The reviewed deployment guidance distinguishes commercial, GCC High, DoD and 21Vianet Graph endpoints and cloud-specific tokens. A connection should use the endpoint and identity context of the modeled cloud; downstream workloads remain distinct data and authorization boundaries.

Risks
Review the requested resource, token audience and effective permissions, including whether a call acts as a user or application. A successful call to Graph does not establish that access to every downstream workload is intended.

Uncertainty
The target APIs, permission grants and deployment cloud are not observed. This entry does not inherit Data Connect's infrastructure or national-cloud availability; use feature-specific evidence before modeling that separate data-export path.

label: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/what-is-defender-for-cloud-apps).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Defender for Cloud Apps is a SaaS security service. The discovery or connector path selected for a model is distinct from the monitored application's own hosting boundary.

Dependencies
The reviewed Cloud Discovery guidance permits a customer-hosted log collector or a separately enabled feed from onboarded Defender for Endpoint devices. The MDE feed does not require a separate collector or traffic mirroring; do not create both dependency paths automatically.

Risks
Review which sources actually provide telemetry, who can administer collection and what sensitive activity data is transferred. Visibility of a service in a security portal does not prove complete coverage of applications or users.

Uncertainty
The discovery mode, onboarding and connector capabilities are unspecified. Apply only the selected path's requirements and keep collection, API governance and session-control capabilities separate; none establishes that a particular application is securely configured.

label: Windows 365
description: Windows 365 catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-365/overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Windows 365 is the Cloud PC product, distinct from an Azure Virtual Desktop host-pool resource or a generic Azure VM. Product edition matters.

Dependencies
The reviewed Windows 365 Enterprise guidance says provisioned Cloud PCs automatically enroll in Intune, where administrators manage provisioning policies, configuration, applications and updates for Entra-joined and hybrid-joined PCs. This is an Enterprise-scoped relationship, not a statement about every edition.

Risks
Review who can configure the Cloud PC and what identities, applications and data it can reach. Managed provisioning should not be mistaken for proof that device policies, application permissions or data-access paths match the user's task.

Uncertainty
Edition, join mode, selected network and actual management settings are unknown. Customer-network and hybrid-directory prerequisites need their own evidence; do not assume a customer VNet or domain controller for every Windows 365 node.

label: Universal Print
description: Universal Print catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/universal-print/fundamentals/universal-print-whatis).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Universal Print is the cloud print service; physical printers and any installed connector are separate components rather than one cloud-only data boundary.

Dependencies
For the Windows connector path, the reviewed documentation says a temporary job file may be stored locally. The connector attempts deletion after spooler submission, but exceptional failures can require administrator deletion. Cloud service data protection does not remove that separate local-copy consideration.

Risks
Review the content sent to print, who can release or retrieve it and how connector-host copies are handled after errors. Treating successful cloud submission as proof that every copy was removed could overlook residual documents.

Uncertainty
The printer, connector use, host protection and actual job state are unknown. Do not assume every printer requires the connector or that service retention alone describes spooler, device and physical-output handling.

label: Microsoft Whiteboard
description: Microsoft Whiteboard catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/whiteboard/whiteboard-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft Whiteboard is the collaboration workload. A board's hosting generation matters; modern OneDrive-backed boards and legacy Azure Whiteboards must not be treated as one evidenced storage path.

Dependencies
For a OneDrive-stored Whiteboard, reviewed guidance says its content location follows the creator's OneDrive location. That scoped statement does not establish the location or migration state of a legacy Azure Whiteboard.

Risks
Review who creates and shares a board and what participant information or business content it contains. Assuming a meeting's audience or tenant location automatically describes the board's permissions and storage can leave a distinct collaboration boundary unexamined.

Uncertainty
The actual board generation, creator location, sharing and retention settings are unknown. Do not infer that every board has moved to OneDrive or that the cited location relationship proves compliance with a particular residency requirement.

label: Microsoft Loop
description: Microsoft Loop catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/loop/loop-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft Loop is a collaboration product with components and workspaces used through different experiences. The containing host is relevant to the guidance applied to an item.

Dependencies
The reviewed requirements distinguish cloud availability by integration: US government clouds support Teams components but not Loop workspaces or the other listed integrations. Support for one Loop surface therefore does not establish support for all of them.

Risks
Review the host, participants and sharing scope for the actual component or workspace. Treating every Loop object as the same supported experience could hide an unsupported workflow or a separate content-access boundary.

Uncertainty
The host integration, cloud, item location and configured access are unknown. This entry does not establish a universal storage deployment or require every Loop integration; use the selected experience's requirements and retain unsupported branch details as unknown.

label: Viva Engage
description: Viva Engage catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/engage/overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Viva Engage is the community and communications product. Legacy Yammer endpoint hints do not define its complete current network or service-plan boundary.

Dependencies
The reviewed network guidance requires access to engage.cloud.microsoft and recommends against reliance on static IP allowlists. Setup also distinguishes core, premium communications/community and Knowledge/Answers service plans; the chosen plan affects available capabilities.

Risks
Review the intended community audience and the network path used to reach the service. A historic domain matcher or broad community membership should not be treated as evidence of complete connectivity or appropriate disclosure of posted content.

Uncertainty
The service plan, community membership, sharing and actual endpoint configuration are unknown. Do not assume every premium feature is enabled or use a static address list from this guidance; current endpoint details remain a configuration-specific source check.

label: Microsoft Purview
description: Microsoft Purview catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/purview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
This entry represents the Microsoft Purview compliance/governance product family, not the separate Azure Microsoft.Purview/accounts resource or one universal enforcement service.

Dependencies
The reviewed service description assigns different entitlements to base and advanced DLP, information-protection and other Purview capabilities. A suite name or portal entry does not select the feature, its supported workload or its configuration.

Risks
Review which data location and action a chosen feature actually covers, who sets the policy and how exceptions are handled. A label, license or visible policy should not be treated as evidence that every endpoint, collaboration workload or export path is protected.

Uncertainty
The selected feature, entitlement and effective policy are unknown. Keep capability-specific setup and billing relationships conditional; no shared authoring group or catalog policy field establishes compliance or activates a Purview control.

label: SharePoint in Microsoft 365
description: SharePoint in Microsoft 365 catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/introduction).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
SharePoint in Microsoft 365 is the organizational cloud content workload, not SharePoint Server or an automatic alias for every OneDrive data path.

Dependencies
The reviewed commercial-cloud guidance requires platform-enabled Entra B2B integration for new external sharing and distinguishes retirement of SharePoint OTP from continued support for Entra email OTP. Those are separate mechanisms, not a blanket end to all one-time-passcode access.

Risks
Review the site and item audience, guest identity and sharing permission rather than treating identity integration as sufficient authorization. A guest's ability to authenticate does not establish that an item should be disclosed to that guest.

Uncertainty
The cloud, existing sharing state, effective permissions and rollout behavior are not observed. Archived transition statements are not evidence that a specific tenant completed a change, and they should not be generalized to every government or historical sharing scenario.

label: Microsoft 365 Apps
description: Microsoft 365 Apps catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/office-applications-service-description/office-applications-service-description).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft 365 Apps is an application suite with installed clients and service integrations, not one SaaS resource or the same scope as Office for the web.

Dependencies
The reviewed deployment guidance supports Intune and Configuration Manager as alternative customer-managed methods, with architecture, existing-MSI and update-channel considerations. Neither management method is a mandatory dependency for every catalog instance.

Risks
Review who controls installation and updates, which client configuration is applied and what service or add-in receives document content. Treating suite deployment as a single server-side control can overlook client and extension boundaries.

Uncertainty
The installed applications, deployment method, channel, entitlement and actual policies are unknown. Browser and desktop features are not presumed equivalent, and choosing an authoring group does not supply endpoint protection, information-protection or data-handling policy.

label: Microsoft Intune
description: Microsoft Intune catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/what-is-intune).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft Intune is the cloud management service; devices, certificate authorities and installed connectors remain distinct components in a design.

Dependencies
If the Certificate Connector is selected, reviewed guidance distinguishes the licensed Intune Administrator used for Entra registration from its Windows service identity and feature-specific certificate permissions. SCEP additionally has an NDES application-pool identity. These are conditional certificate-integration roles, not universal Intune dependencies.

Risks
Review which identity can register the connector, request certificates and administer its host. Collapsing them into one service account can hide different privilege and recovery responsibilities.

Uncertainty
No certificate connector, SCEP path, device enrollment or service identity has been observed. Use only the configured integration's requirements, and do not infer that an Intune tenant automatically supplies every device or certificate-management control.

label: Microsoft Defender for Office 365
description: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/mdo-about).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Defender for Office 365 is a workload-protection product, distinct from Exchange Online mailboxes, Exchange Online Protection and the broader Defender XDR platform.

Dependencies
For Safe Attachments email scanning, the reviewed documentation describes detonation in a virtual environment in the same region where Microsoft 365 data resides. This is a specific scanning path, not a complete statement about every Defender feature or customer content flow.

Risks
Review which mailboxes and message routes are actually covered and what actions the configured policy takes. The existence of a scanning capability should not be treated as proof of policy enablement, recipient authorization or protection of unrelated collaboration content.

Uncertainty
The entitlement, applicable policies, exclusions and actual message path are unknown. Do not infer a customer-owned sandbox or new Azure infrastructure from the documented scanning environment; service behavior is not an attestation about a tenant.

label: Exchange Online Archiving
description: Exchange Online Archiving catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-archiving-service-description/exchange-online-archiving-service-description).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Exchange Online Archiving is an archive capability, not a standalone replacement for the primary mailbox or a general-purpose data store.

Dependencies
The reviewed service description makes the associated mailbox arrangement significant: a cloud archive for an on-premises primary mailbox requires supported Exchange hybrid configuration. Archiving availability also varies by plan and by the Exchange Server versus Exchange Online arrangement.

Risks
Review which mailbox and archive are associated, who can search them and how retention, deletion or hold requirements apply. An archive's presence does not establish that every message is retained or that access and discovery permissions are appropriate.

Uncertainty
The mailbox location, assigned plan, hybrid setup and actual retention/hold configuration are unknown. Do not add an on-premises Exchange server for a cloud-primary-mailbox scenario or treat an archiving feature as proof of regulatory compliance.

label: Exchange Online Protection
description: Exchange Online Protection catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-protection-service-description/exchange-online-protection-service-description).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Exchange Online Protection represents mail protection, not the mailbox store or every Defender for Office 365 capability. Cloud mailbox protection and the on-premises add-on have different routing contexts.

Dependencies
For the documented on-premises path, the customer configures domains/MX and bidirectional connectors, including smart-host delivery, server identification and SMTP reachability. This setup must not be imposed on all Exchange Online mailbox deployments.

Risks
Review the trusted sending and receiving systems and whether a message can take a route outside the intended protection path. A connector or MX record alone does not prove that all inbound and outbound mail follows the modeled route.

Uncertainty
The mailbox hosting arrangement, connector restrictions and observed routing are not supplied. Product naming changes do not establish that protection was retired or enabled; apply the referenced configuration only to the selected mail-flow scenario.

label: Viva Connections
description: Viva Connections catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/connections/viva-connections-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Viva Connections is an employee-experience capability that can be associated with different intranet and host arrangements, not a universal pre-existing portal deployment.

Dependencies
The reviewed setup supports both a new standalone experience and an existing intranet-portal path. An existing SharePoint home site is not a universal prerequisite, so it should not be added to every model merely because Connections is present.

Risks
Review the actual content sources and audience of the experience, including whether links expose material beyond the intended employee group. An integrated navigation surface does not establish identical permissions across all linked destinations.

Uncertainty
The chosen experience, host, content sources and sharing configuration are unknown. Only add an intranet or other service relationship when the scenario establishes it; this capability's presence is not proof that all underlying sites or applications have been reviewed.

label: Microsoft Viva
description: Microsoft Viva catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/microsoft-viva-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Microsoft Viva is a family of employee-experience applications, not a separately established deployment with a uniform data or security contract.

Dependencies
Reviewed setup documentation provides a Viva hub with per-app settings and identifies Engage as an exception to setup from that admin page. The compliance documentation explicitly conditions shared controls on the individual Viva application.

Risks
Review which constituent app actually receives employee data and which team administers that experience. Applying a statement from one module to the entire suite can obscure different processing purposes, data paths and permissions.

Uncertainty
The constituent modules, licenses and enabled integrations are not specified. Keep this entry at family scope until the model names the relevant branch; neither a Viva license nor a shared authoring template proves an inherited policy, dependency or compliance outcome.

label: Viva Glint
description: Viva Glint catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/glint/introduction-viva-glint).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Viva Glint is the employee-feedback product, separate from Viva Pulse and the general Viva family. Survey participation and tenant provisioning are different concerns.

Dependencies
The reviewed provisioning guidance requires at least 50 active licenses and a directly assigned tenant Global Administrator. Its base licensing counts active users rather than requiring individual assignment. The reviewed residency material also describes region-specific processing and configurable retention.

Risks
Review access to employee responses and reports and whether the chosen reporting audience could expose sensitive feedback. A provisioning role or license count does not establish an appropriate survey audience or retention setting.

Uncertainty
The tenant configuration and region are not observed, and archived region lists are inconsistent across sources. Do not resolve that public-documentation conflict through a customer assumption or treat a selected region as proof of all processing locations.

label: Viva Pulse
description: Viva Pulse catalog entry from Microsoft 365. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/pulse/introduction-to-viva-pulse).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Viva Pulse is the lightweight feedback product, not Viva Glint or a generic survey infrastructure service. The Teams-hosted and web experiences are distinct access paths.

Dependencies
The reviewed prerequisites require Teams deployment for the Teams experience while also describing a web experience without Teams. Administrative responsibilities are divided among Microsoft 365 Global Administrator, Viva Pulse Administrator and Teams Administrator roles for the applicable setup actions.

Risks
Review who can administer feedback settings, send requests and see the resulting information. Treating app installation as equivalent to authority over employee feedback could hide a separate privacy or administrative boundary.

Uncertainty
The selected experience, administrators, audience and feedback configuration are unknown. Teams is not asserted as a universal dependency for all Pulse use, and the presence of a role or entitlement does not prove that permissions and data practices suit the modeled scenario.

label: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

The selected hierarchy members, optional components, workload resources and feature use are unknown. Preserve the composite scope without imposing one layer’s dependencies on every deployment; verify feature availability and controls against the actual configuration.

Choose the architecture that matches the workload: globally through Azure Front Door, regionally through Application Gateway, or for Kubernetes workloads through Application Gateway for Containers. Review host coverage, listener/domain association, rule mode, exclusions, logging and origin reachability. A WAF policy that is unattached, bypassable, or incomplete for an alternate route does not protect that traffic; WAF does not replace identity, authorization or network controls.

Uncertainty
The WAF host, tier, cloud/region availability, policy configuration and observed traffic path are unknown. Confirm current feature support and that every intended public entry point traverses the configured policy; the catalog does not verify deployment.

Review client reachability, protocol-specific identity and authorization, data copies and backup/recovery separately for the selected model. Private connectivity alone does not prove data authorization, and SMB-specific guidance does not automatically apply to NFS.

Uncertainty
The concrete provider, protocol, account/share configuration, region, permissions and deployment evidence are unknown. The cloud, region, workloads and enabled controls are unknown. Do not infer one universal networking or storage recipe across the platform, and keep the cited feature matrix separate from an assessment of any deployed workspace.

label: Fabric Data Engineering
description: Fabric Data Engineering catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-engineering/data-engineering-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Fabric Data Engineering is the workload/item family for lakehouse, notebook and Spark-related work, not a customer-managed Azure VM deployment.

Dependencies
Reviewed Spark pool guidance lets capacity administrators standardize pool settings and restrict workspace customization, with custom sizing and autoscale/executor bounds controlled administratively. Available customization does not establish the settings of an actual job or pool.

Risks
Review who can change execution settings and what data a notebook or job can read, transform and export. A governed compute configuration should not be mistaken for evidence that the code or its data permissions are appropriate.

Uncertainty
The item, pool policy, execution identity and network path are unknown. Do not infer that every item has triggered managed-VNet allocation or that a shared workspace gives all users the same authority; each execution and data path needs scoped evidence.

label: Fabric Data Factory
description: Fabric Data Factory catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-factory/data-factory-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
This is Data Factory in Fabric, not the Azure Microsoft.DataFactory/factories resource. Pipelines, copy jobs and Dataflow Gen2 are different execution surfaces.

Dependencies
Reviewed Azure SQL and ADLS Gen2 connector tables provide different authentication sets for Dataflow Gen2 versus Pipeline/Copy Job. A service-principal or workspace-identity option in one surface must not be applied to every connector or connection.

Risks
Review the exact connector, execution surface and identity used for each source and destination. A connection that works for one activity does not prove that another activity supports the same permissions or accesses the same data boundary.

Uncertainty
Connectors, credentials, gateway use and target configuration are unknown. Do not automatically add a gateway or infer universal authentication parity; apply only the selected source/sink and execution-path requirements.

label: Fabric Data Science
description: Fabric Data Science catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-science/overview/).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Fabric Data Science includes ML models and experiments as well as applicable compute experiences. Item management/execution and OneLake data access are distinct boundaries.

Dependencies
Reviewed workspace guidance allows all four workspace roles to view ML model/experiment content and output, while write/delete and execute/cancel are limited to Admin, Member and Contributor. These rights are separate from OneLake data-plane security.

Risks
Review both the information exposed by model/experiment outputs and the authority to execute or change an item. A read-oriented workspace role can still reveal sensitive output, while execution permission does not establish appropriate access to every source dataset.

Uncertainty
The items, workspace roles, source-data permissions and network path are unknown. Do not infer that all ML processing uses one managed VNet or that a workspace role alone describes the full training, output and data-access boundary.

label: Fabric Data Warehouse
description: Fabric Data Warehouse catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-warehouse/overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Fabric Warehouse is the workload boundary, not Azure SQL or Synapse dedicated SQL merely because each exposes SQL concepts.

Dependencies
Reviewed access guidance supports narrowly scoped item-plus-SQL-object grants rather than making every consumer a Contributor. SQL auditing is separately enabled with selected actions, predicate and retention, producing OneLake audit files in the documented path.

Risks
Review workspace roles and SQL object permissions together, then check whether the chosen audit scope captures the operations of interest. A permissive workspace role or the existence of an audit capability should not be treated as evidence of least privilege or active logging.

Uncertainty
Actual grants, audit configuration and data access are unknown. Do not infer a customer storage account, uniform row-level policy or automatic auditing for every warehouse; supported controls still require configuration and instance evidence.

label: Fabric Databases
description: Fabric Databases catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/database/).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Fabric Databases is a database/mirroring workload family, not a single external source or one universal replication network path.

Dependencies
For the reviewed private Cosmos DB mirroring branch, source setup needs its documented authentication and network preparation. Ongoing replication uses Microsoft's internal network rather than the customer gateway/private endpoint used for setup. That distinction must not be generalized to every mirrored source.

Risks
Review what is replicated, which principal enables access and where source and replica permissions differ. A setup connection alone does not describe the ongoing data path or prove that copied data retains the intended access and lifecycle.

Uncertainty
The database item, mirroring source, credentials and configuration are unknown. Do not infer a gateway for all replication, apply Cosmos networking to SQL or other providers, or treat a mirrored copy as evidence of complete source-data governance.

label: Fabric Real-Time Intelligence
description: Fabric Real-Time Intelligence catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/real-time-intelligence/overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Real-Time Intelligence is the Fabric Eventstream/Eventhouse/KQL workload family, not one uniform streaming deployment or storage policy.

Dependencies
Reviewed KQL guidance separates data-retention from caching and prevents caching from exceeding retention. Eventstream Private Link has a source/destination matrix and REST-only creation/management in the documented setup; not every destination path is supported.

Risks
Review where an event is ingested, transformed and retained, and whether the selected path supports the intended private connection. A cache setting or private endpoint should not be mistaken for the full data lifecycle or universal Eventstream compatibility.

Uncertainty
Item type, destinations, policies and network settings are unknown. Do not infer one retention value across the family or extend a supported Eventhouse preprocessing route to direct ingestion and every other event destination.

label: OneLake
description: OneLake catalog entry from Microsoft Fabric. Authentication and data-handling policies are not yet curated. See [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/onelake/onelake-overview).

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
OneLake is the Fabric data-lake component, not an independently selected Azure Storage account or an internal managed-data-lake alias.

Dependencies
Reviewed workspace controls support direct OneLake/lakehouse/shortcut inbound access through workspace IP firewall rules. Approved-resource rules provide identity-based network admission without granting data permissions; these are configured Fabric controls, not a separate customer-provisioned firewall resource.

Risks
Review which caller is admitted and what data permission that caller has after admission. A trusted resource or allowed address should not be taken as authorization to read every table, folder or shortcut target.

Uncertainty
Workspace configuration, identities, permissions and actual shortcuts are unknown. Do not infer a universal private network or automatic data-protection enforcement, and keep governance visibility distinct from verified access and lifecycle controls.

label: AI Builder
description: Power Platform AI models and prompts used by selected app and automation experiences. It is not the Copilot Studio agent platform or a customer Azure OpenAI deployment.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
AI Builder provides models/prompts, distinct from Copilot Studio agents and Agent 365 governance.

Dependencies
The reviewed prompt architecture uses Dataverse for prompt creation and platform-managed communication to Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Content Safety. This logical path is not a complete network trace or a customer-resource provisioning requirement.

Risks
Review prompt inputs, grounding data, output audience and action permissions. Moderation does not establish that the source data or resulting disclosure is authorized.

Uncertainty
Selected model/feature, identities, endpoints and permissions are unknown. Do not generalize this prompt architecture to every model path or create customer AI resources merely from this guidance.

label: Microsoft Agent 365
description: Cross-product agent observability, governance and security capabilities. It is not Copilot Studio authoring/runtime, Microsoft 365 Copilot itself, or a universal dependency of every agent.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Agent 365 observes, governs and secures agents across products. It is not a substitute for Copilot Studio agent authoring or Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Dependencies
Reviewed management prerequisites include qualifying licenses and suitable administrative roles. Visibility of an agent and authority to manage it are different permissions.

Risks
Review enrolled-agent coverage, who can change management state and the connected workloads each agent can access. A registry entry or governance license is not proof every action is controlled.

Uncertainty
Licenses, roles, enrolled agents and feature/cloud availability are unobserved. Do not require Agent 365 for every agent design or assume all capabilities are enabled.

label: On-premises data gateway
description: Customer-installed gateway connecting supported cloud workloads to selected data sources. Distinguish standard/personal modes and the separate Microsoft-managed VNet data gateway; not every app requires a gateway.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
The on-premises data gateway is customer-hosted Windows infrastructure, not the separate Microsoft-managed VNet data gateway. Identify standard or personal mode.

Dependencies
Selected cloud/data-source integrations may use this gateway. Reviewed communication guidance describes outbound cloud connections and their responses, not a requirement for inbound connections.

Risks
Review host administration, stored source credentials and which cloud workloads can request data. Outbound-only networking does not prove appropriately restricted data-source access.

Uncertainty
Mode, patching, sources and permissions are unknown. Do not impose a gateway on every Power Platform/Fabric app or substitute VNet-gateway provisioning requirements.

label: Power Apps
description: Low-code application platform for canvas and model-driven apps. Model-driven apps use Dataverse; canvas apps use their selected sources and connectors, so Dataverse and on-premises gateways are not universal dependencies.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Distinguish canvas and model-driven Power Apps. Model-driven apps use Dataverse; canvas apps depend on selected sources/connectors, not necessarily Dataverse.

Dependencies
Model only the chosen data connections and any required gateway path. Reviewed SAS IP restrictions govern covered storage access, not a WAF over every player or connector request; proxy/NAT and address-family limitations matter.

Risks
Review app sharing separately from data permissions, connector identities and disclosure to the actual user. A storage IP restriction does not establish protection of all metadata/media/connector traffic.

Uncertainty
App type, sources, connection identities and network settings need evidence. Do not infer universal private ingress, a customer VNet or an on-premises gateway from this product ID.

label: Power Automate
description: Automation platform spanning cloud flows and desktop flows. Desktop machines, unattended execution, connectors and gateway paths have branch-specific requirements rather than a single universal deployment.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Cloud flows and desktop flows have different hosting, identity and execution boundaries.

Dependencies
For desktop execution, use the documented global plus selected-cloud endpoint lists and conditional connector/custom-action requirements. Hosted-machine provisioning has additional endpoints. Machine and unattended-entitlement requirements are not prerequisites of every cloud flow.

Risks
Review the running identity, machine privileges, credentials and systems affected by each selected action. Connectivity or a trigger does not authorize arbitrary automation.

Uncertainty
Execution mode, machine posture, cloud, licensing and connectors are unknown. Do not infer a fixed IP set, universal no-elevation boundary or mandatory desktop/gateway infrastructure.

label: Power Pages
description: Hosted website product for external-facing experiences with Dataverse data. Model the visitor, hosted site and selected backend/agent integrations separately; this is not an on-premises website-hosting product.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Power Pages is a hosted website, distinct from the Power Apps player. For a site summarizing Dataverse data with an agent, identify the intended Copilot product and represent site, agent and data service separately.

Dependencies
Use only selected integrations. When supported native Power Pages WAF is enabled, Power Pages provisions an Azure Front Door profile; this is not an instruction to deploy a separate customer Front Door/WAF resource.

Risks
Review visitor authentication, page/table permissions, agent connection identity and the audience of summaries. WAF traffic inspection does not authorize a data operation or prevent overbroad grounding-data disclosure.

Uncertainty
Agent integration, WAF support/enablement, permissions and routing require confirmation. Do not assume direct ownership of platform-managed infrastructure or that every Power Platform flow shares this perimeter.

label: Microsoft Dataverse
description: Managed business-data platform organized into tables for Power Platform and selected Dynamics applications. Standard, elastic and virtual tables have different storage/access paths; it is not a customer-managed database host.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Dataverse is a managed business-data platform. Distinguish standard, elastic and virtual tables rather than assuming one storage boundary.

Dependencies
Elastic tables use a Dataverse-managed Azure Cosmos DB backend; virtual tables access an external source through a provider at runtime without replication. Neither implies a customer Cosmos DB deployment. Identify the actual site/agent connection and source-security boundary.

Risks
Review table/row/column access, effective caller versus connection identity and which records may be used in a summary. External-source permissions are not established solely by Dataverse row security.

Uncertainty
Table kinds, source credentials, permissions and retention are unobserved. Do not infer a universal storage/retention contract or treat guidance as verified policy. Shared CRM hostnames do not uniquely identify a Dynamics application.

label: Dataverse Table
description: Contained Dataverse table accessed through the parent Dataverse APIs, not a separately hosted database. Table kind determines storage, access and supported auditing behavior.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
A Dataverse table is a contained component accessed through the parent Dataverse APIs, not an independently deployed database or a table-specific hostname.

Dependencies
For the reviewed audit path, environment, table and relevant column auditing must be enabled and changes saved/published. Virtual tables do not support that auditing mechanism and retain an external-source boundary.

Risks
Review row/column content, effective readers and which changes are captured. Environment-level auditing alone does not prove every table/column is audited or suitable for an agent's grounding query.

Uncertainty
Table kind, permissions and audit configuration are unknown. Do not infer separate Azure storage, one retention policy or verified access controls from the table's presence.

label: Dataverse Plugin
description: Registered server-side Dataverse event handler with synchronous or asynchronous execution and possible external calls. It is not a standalone addressed service, nor a guarantee of one shared operating-system process.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
A Dataverse plug-in is registered server-side event-pipeline logic; distinguish synchronous/asynchronous steps and possible outbound calls. Do not assume one shared operating-system process.

Dependencies
Step registration defaults to Calling User but can select another user. Service creation in code can also select an execution identity; initiating-user, registration and service-call identities are not automatically identical.

Risks
Review each effective data-operation identity, privileges and outbound destination, not only the triggering caller. Registration alone does not establish safe authorization or prevent data disclosure.

Uncertainty
Registration, code, permissions and external integrations are unobserved. No default VNet, customer storage or dependency node is implied; verify execution context against actual configuration and code.

label: Microsoft Copilot Studio
description: Low-code authoring and management of AI-powered agents and workflows, with selected channels, knowledge and actions. Distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent 365 governance.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Copilot Studio authors/manages agents and workflows. It is distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent 365 governance. For an ambiguous 'Copilot' request, ask which product and integration are intended instead of substituting Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Dependencies
Model only selected channels, knowledge sources and actions. A Power Pages/Dataverse summarization design needs an explicit site-to-agent path and an authorized data-access path; choose the supported integration and identity rather than assuming a particular connector or custom Azure resource.

Risks
Review user/channel authentication, connection-owner versus caller permissions, grounding-data audience, prompt injection and action authorization. A generated summary is not evidence or permission to disclose every retrieved record.

Uncertainty
Channel support, data integration, licensing, retention and effective identities require confirmation. Do not auto-create Agent 365, Azure OpenAI, AI Search or connector dependencies from the product label.

label: Power Platform connectors
description: Connector-family abstraction for selected Power Platform integrations with data and service APIs. Specify the connector, connection identity and backend; this is not one universal environment API or deployment.

aiDesignGuidance.content:
Context
Power Platform connectors are an integration family, not one universal API or hosting boundary. Name the selected connector and backend in the model.

Dependencies
An actual connection, its authentication/authorization and the selected backend determine the path. Confirm whether that connector needs a gateway or supports private networking; neither is universal across the family.

Risks
Review connection-owner versus caller privileges, allowed operations, data-policy grouping and data crossing into the backend. Availability in a connector list is not approval, configured access or proof of every backend's security.

Uncertainty
Connector/operation, ownership, licensing, gateway/network support and effective permissions are unknown. Do not equate this family with a private environment-connectivity API or automatically add all possible infrastructure.
